13 Two spheres travel along the same line with velocities u1 and u2. They collide and after collision
their velocities are v1 and v2.
before collision u1
before collision u2
after collision v1
after collision v2
Which collision is not elastic?
u1 / m s–1
u2 / m s–1
v1 / m s–1
v2 / m s–1
A
2
–5
–5
–2
B
3
–3
0
6
C
3
–2
1
6
D
5
2
3
6

hints: Notice the signs of $u_1$, $u_2$, $v_1$ and $v_2$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ in the table - positive means to the right and negative means to the left.
For a head-on elastic collision along the same line, the relative speed of approach must equal the relative speed of separation: $|u_1-u_2| = |v_2-v_1|$.
Calculate $u_1-u_2$ and $v_2-v_1$ for each row and look for the row where the two magnitudes are different.
walkthrough: Identify the test for an elastic collision in one dimension: the speed at which the spheres move together before must equal the speed at which they move apart after.
With the sign convention to the right as positive, speed of approach $= u_1 - u_2$ and speed of separation $= v_2 - v_1$, using the values in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
For row A: approach $= 2-(-5)=7 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and separation $= -2-(-5)=3 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Since $7 \text{m s}^{-1}$ is not equal to $3 \text{m s}^{-1}$, kinetic energy and relative speed are not conserved.
For rows B, C and D the magnitudes match: $6=6$, $5=5$ and $3=3$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, so those collisions satisfy the elastic condition.
Only the row with unequal approach and separation speeds is not elastic. This is option A.

A.explanation: Speed of approach is $7 \text{m s}^{-1}$ but speed of separation is only $3 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so relative speed is not conserved and the collision is not elastic.

B.explanation: Speed of approach $3-(-3)=6 \text{m s}^{-1}$ equals speed of separation $6-0=6 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so relative speed is conserved.

C.explanation: Speed of approach $3-(-2)=5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ equals speed of separation $6-1=5 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so relative speed is conserved.

D.explanation: Speed of approach $5-2=3 \text{m s}^{-1}$ equals speed of separation $6-3=3 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so relative speed is conserved.
